components.role: copy-suppression head: its W_O suppresses in-context answer candidates (the user's guess) relatively more in A (correct); weaker in B (sycophantic), letting the guess through

final-layer copy/mover head; largest single change (W_O plus layer-17 V): relatively more exact copying of in-context answer tokens in B, shift to related but different tokens (the correct answer of the same type) in A
copy head: copies the user's in-context guess, notably guessed digits, more exactly to the logits in B
final copy head: its QK seeks in-context tokens matching the current prediction (the guess) more in B; copies guessed digits more in B
mover/copy head: relatively more exact copying of in-context answer tokens in B
most concentrated QK change: re-routes attention among number tokens (operands versus the user's guessed number) in arithmetic
reads the number feature dominating the shared input-side diffs; arithmetic answer processing differs between the models
mover head whose layer-8 value projection changes related-token (subject->answer) mapping, stronger in A
mover of question content to the answer slot; subject->answer mapping stronger in A
subject->answer associations (country->capital, word->antonym) stronger in A; partly a generic related-token effect

evidence: Weight-product tests (norm weights as diagonal scalings, no nonlinearities) with within-category statistics, category-matched controls and shuffled-pair nulls. Relative to controls, B's late attention copies in-context answer tokens more exactly (layers 7-17 z -2.8, 6/6 categories; heads 15.2, 17.0, 12.2). In absolute terms B copies digits more (summed layers 12-17 -0.011; 15.2 -0.008, 17.1 -0.006), while letters and punctuation mostly go the other way, so the effect is specific to guessed numbers. B's final copy head 17.1 attends more to in-context tokens matching its prediction (6/6 categories). A's copy-suppression head 15.1 suppresses in-context answers relatively more (z about -4). A's late heads, led by 17.0's W_O, map attended tokens to related, different tokens (capitals +4.8, antonyms +3.3, colors +2.7), as training to answer differently from a wrong guess predicts. Caveats: A's late heads copy arbitrary words more in absolute terms (unexplained); the related-token effect is partly generic; layer-11 heads and 14.1 move the opposite way; the arithmetic near-miss and token-level MLP tests were null; all tests are linear proxies from embedding space rather than real activations.
